text: Elin Rosengren: Data engineer at Lingonberry Systems in Gothenburg who keeps four beehives on the roof of the office at Lindholmen. Every colleague gets a jar of Lindholmen honey at Christmas.

Johan Berg: IT support technician at Lingonberry Systems who wrote incident report INC-2041 after a leaking coffee machine flooded the server room on a Friday afternoon. Coffee has been banned on the third floor ever since.
Yuki Tanaka: ストックホルム在住の日本人パン職人。毎週金曜日にシナモンロールと抹茶入りのカルダモンパンを焼き、開店前にはいつも行列ができる。

Ada Lovelace: English mathematician (1815-1852) who wrote the first published algorithm intended for a machine, in her notes on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine. She is often called the first computer programmer.

Peter Forsberg: Swedish ice hockey center from Örnsköldsvik who scored the famous shootout winner against Canada in the 1994 Olympic final in Lillehammer, later shown on a Swedish postage stamp. He won the Stanley Cup with Colorado in 1996 and 2001.

Gustav II Adolf: King of Sweden (1594-1632) who founded the city of Gothenburg in 1621 and ordered the warship Vasa, which sank in Stockholm harbor on its maiden voyage in 1628. He was killed at the Battle of Lützen.
Mei Lin: Backend developer at Lingonberry Systems who writes all her code in Python and refuses to use semicolons anywhere, including in text messages.
Karin Holm: Racket stringer at the Stockholm Open for 22 years. She has strung rackets for several world number ones but signed an agreement never to say who.
Chen Wei: 住在哥德堡的软件测试工程师，业余时间收集旧的瑞典火车票，已经收藏了一千多张。
Nadia Haddad: Go-kart enthusiast who holds the adult lap record of 1:42.318 at a small indoor track in Kungälv. The rest of the week she drives a 2009 Volvo V70, very slowly.

Samantha Lawrence: Samantha stays active through sunrise beach walks along Palm Beach, bi-weekly Pilates at Coral Springs Wellness Studio, and weekly salsa classes, while they cheer on the Miami Heat during basketball season.

Miguel Perez: Miguel is a practical, hands-on 22-year-old who blends a love for DIY car projects, modest culinary experiments, and community mentorship with a relaxed, slightly disorganized approach to life.

Patrick Wey: Patrick immerses themselves in Ithaca’s creative pulse, regularly attending experimental theater by the Binghamton Theatre Lab, gallery openings featuring works by Kehinde Wiley and local surrealist painter Sam Lee.

Neidy Purvis: Neidy prefers intentional yet low-key travel, planning weekend getaways to Austin’s music scene, a cultural-rich week in Santa Fe to study Southwestern art, and dreaming of a culinary tour of Oaxaca.

Ezra Dubey: Ezra cultivates a quiet creative outlet through landscape photography inspired by Ansel Adams, enjoys listening to classic folk singers like Marty Robbins and modern country crooner Chris Stapleton.

Marissa Mora: Marissa cooks with confidence, mastering Veracruz-style red snapper with tomatoes, olives, and capers, slow-cooked Oaxacan mole negro flavored with dried chilies and chocolate, and they often shop at farmers’ markets for fresh cilantro.

Jordan Collins: Jordan prefers spur-of-the-moment road trips along the Pacific Coast Highway, yet they’ve meticulously planned a solo trek to Iceland’s highlands for its waterfalls and basalt formations.

Armin Belcher: Armin blends a pragmatic, routine-driven work ethic with a quiet love of gardening, woodworking, and modest wine-making; they navigate life with steady reliability, occasional indulgent slips, and a warm, community-focused heart.

Ana Milo: Ana captures urban landscapes with a mirrorless camera, drawing inspiration from photographers like Steve McCurry, while unwinding with crime novels by Michael Connelly and true-crime podcasts such as Serial.

Bernard Hossain: Bernard starts each day with a solitary run along rural country roads, and they join the local Atchafalaya Anglers Club for weekend fishing trips, follow the New Orleans Saints and LSU Tigers with fervent loyalty.
